title: Finite-parameter guarantees for fixed-lifetime perishable inventory
short_statement: Simple policies already have approximation and large-penalty optimality guarantees. The remaining target is sharper nonasymptotic control or exact structure at finite parameters, not the mere existence of asymptotic results.
open_problem: For the specified FIFO lost-sales model at fixed finite parameters, establish a useful exact policy structure or sharper explicit performance bounds for a tractable policy. Exclude already settled high-penalty demand regimes and specify the benchmark and computational guarantees.
background: Age composition matters because two inventories with the same total stock can have very different future expiry losses. The oldest-first rule fixes issuance, leaving the order decision as the control. This creates a genuine multidimensional dynamic program even with one item and zero lead time. The policy literature now offers more than heuristics: approximation algorithms and high-penalty asymptotic theorems explain when relatively simple policies work. A useful open question must therefore isolate what these theorems leave unresolved. Here that is exact structure and finite-parameter performance outside the proved regimes. The positive-lead-time extension has additional pipeline information and a separate recent projected-inventory-level literature; its results should not be confused with the zero-lead-time baseline.
full_statement:
Consider periodic-review inventory of a single item with fixed shelf life $m\ge3$, zero replenishment lead time, no order-capacity or setup cost, iid nonnegative demand $D_t$ of finite positive mean, and lost sales. At the start of a period the age vector $(x_1,\ldots,x_{m-1})$ gives stock with $1,\ldots,m-1$ periods of remaining life. A nonnegative order arrives immediately with $m$ periods of life. Demand is served oldest first (FIFO). Unmet demand $L_t$ is lost; leftover stock $O_t$ with one period of life expires. Let $H_t$ be all stock remaining after demand and before expiry. The cost is $hH_t+wO_t+pL_t$, with $h,p>0$ and $w\ge0$. Remaining units age by one period.

Starting empty, minimize $\limsup_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\mathbb E\sum_{t=1}^T(hH_t+wO_t+pL_t)$ over nonanticipative ordering policies. A base-stock policy orders $(S-\sum_a x_a)^+$.

The remaining question is an exact structural characterization or a tractable policy with sharper explicit finite-parameter error bounds across this model. State the dependence on $m$, costs, and the demand distribution, and provide a proved computation guarantee for any parameters to be tuned. Large-$p$ optimality in several demand classes is already known and is not, by itself, a new resolution. Positive lead time adds a pipeline to the state and is a separate extension.
known_results:
Classical work by Nahmias and Pierskalla and Nahmias's survey develops age-profile dynamic programming and short-lifetime special cases. Zhang, Ayer, and White's approximation work gives factor-two guarantees under its FIFO-optimality and finite-horizon assumptions; such a finite-horizon bound should not be silently treated as an infinite-horizon average-cost theorem.

Bu, Gong, and Chao (Operations Research 72(5):1765-1774, 2024), Section 4 and Theorem 3, establish large-penalty asymptotics for zero-lead-time perishable inventory, including the iid lost-sales specialization above. For unbounded demand with $\mathbb E[D-x\mid D>x]=o(x)$, the best base-stock cost is asymptotically optimal; Theorem 3(b) also covers continuously distributed regularly varying tails with exponent greater than one. Proposition 5 gives stronger bounded-demand conclusions, including exact optimality at sufficiently large penalty for bounded integer-valued demand. Thus even some finite-parameter cases are settled.

Bu, Gong, and Yin's Management Science article, published online August 26, 2026, studies the different positive-lead-time model. Its publisher abstract reports large-penalty PIL optimality for specified unbounded-demand classes and special bounded-demand results. The full theorem assumptions were not accessible in this pass, so no universal claim for arbitrary demand, lead time, or issuance is made here.

Remaining open problem. Obtain sharper finite-parameter guarantees or exact structure outside the established regimes; do not ask whether any asymptotically optimal simple policy exists.

progress.summary: Published 2024 results prove base-stock optimality in several large-penalty regimes, including some exact bounded-demand cases. A 2026 Management Science paper adds positive-lead-time PIL results; its abstract was screened, not its full theorems.

counterexample_rationale: Small finite-support demand instances with $m=3$ or $4$ can refute proposed base-stock, total-inventory, or critical-number structures through exact dynamic programming. A positive theorem must handle the unbounded age-profile state.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search can map optimal actions for truncated MDPs and find counterexamples to conjectured monotonicity or low-dimensional policies. It can also optimize candidate heuristic parameters, but proofs need dynamic-programming or convexity arguments.

literature.synthesis: The former statement combined exact optimality with existence of any asymptotically optimal policy, leaving the latter incorrectly presented as unexplored. Bu, Gong, and Chao provide explicit average-cost asymptotics in the zero-lead-time model. Approximation algorithms answer a different finite-horizon question, while Bu, Gong, and Yin address positive lead times and more general issuance. These are complementary results with distinct assumptions. The remaining target is a nonasymptotic theorem or exact policy structure for a fixed, specified model, not an unqualified statement that perishability prevents all simple policies from being optimal.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Start with $m=3$ finite-support demand and compute exact discounted or average-cost optimal actions on truncated state spaces. Test conjectures about monotonicity, Schur-convexity in the age profile, or dominance by total inventory plus oldest stock. For approximation, try primal-dual or balancing arguments that improve the factor-2 analysis.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Specify the zero-lead-time FIFO lost-sales average-cost model, including the holding-before-expiry convention. Do not report a known large-penalty limit as new. Transfer of a finite-horizon approximation theorem to average cost needs justification. Positive-lead-time PIL claims require their own assumptions.
